title: Testing and code quality
audience: a computer science graduate or an experienced self-taught programmer preparing for and starting a software engineering job
purpose: Write code that stays correct and readable: kinds of tests and the testing pyramid, unit tests in the pytest style, test-driven development, edge cases, test doubles and mocking, testing code that uses files, time and networks, property-based testing, coverage and mutation testing, readable code and style, type hints and static checking, refactoring and code review.
primary_reading: Test-Driven Development with Python, "Obey the Testing Goat" (free online)

weeks.1: Why test: kinds of tests and the testing pyramid
weeks.2: Unit tests in the pytest style
weeks.4: Test design: edge cases and boundaries
weeks.5: Test doubles: stubs, fakes and mocks
weeks.6: Testing code with dependencies: files, time and networks
weeks.9: Readable code: naming, functions and style

blocks.deliverable: Write tests for five supplied functions.
Test a function that uses the clock and a web API.
Week 7 midterm; find a bug with a property-based test.
Add type hints and fix the errors a checker finds.
Refactor a supplied legacy module under tests.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Legacy rescue: take a supplied untested, messy Python module, write characterization tests, refactor it into clean, typed, well-named code without changing its behavior, add new features test-first, and write a code-review style summary of the changes.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
